title: AWS CLI & SDK
subtitle: Control all of AWS from the terminal — querying resources, scripting infrastructure, and using the SDK in code

content.code:
# Install (Linux/macOS)
curl 'https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-x86_64.zip' -o aws.zip
unzip aws.zip && sudo ./aws/install
aws --version   # aws-cli/2.x.x

# Configure default profile
aws configure
# AWS Access Key ID [None]: AKIA...
# AWS Secret Access Key [None]: xxxxxxxx
# Default region name [None]: ap-south-1    ← your closest region
# Default output format [None]: json

# Stored in:
# ~/.aws/credentials  — keys (never commit this)
# ~/.aws/config       — region, output format

# Named profiles (for multiple accounts)
aws configure --profile production
aws configure --profile staging

# Use a specific profile
aws s3 ls --profile production
export AWS_PROFILE=production   # set for the shell session

# Verify which identity you're using
aws sts get-caller-identity
# { "UserId": "AIDA...", "Account": "123456789012", "Arn": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:user/alice" }

content.filename: AWS CLI reference — most useful commands
content.code:
# ── S3 ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
aws s3 ls                                  # list buckets
aws s3 ls s3://my-bucket/                  # list contents
aws s3 cp file.txt s3://my-bucket/         # upload
aws s3 cp s3://my-bucket/file.txt ./       # download
aws s3 sync ./dist s3://my-bucket/         # sync directory (like rsync)
aws s3 rm s3://my-bucket/file.txt          # delete
aws s3 mb s3://new-bucket-name             # make bucket
aws s3 rb s3://bucket --force              # remove bucket (force = empty first)

# ── EC2 ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
aws ec2 describe-instances                 # list all instances
aws ec2 describe-instances \
  --filters Name=instance-state-name,Values=running  # only running
aws ec2 start-instances --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0
aws ec2 stop-instances --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0
aws ec2 describe-instance-types --instance-types t3.micro t3.small

# ── Lambda ──────────────────────────────────────────────
aws lambda list-functions                  # list functions
aws lambda invoke \
  --function-name my-function \
  --payload '{"key":"value"}' \
  response.json                            # invoke a function
aws lambda get-function --function-name my-function  # get details

# ── IAM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
aws iam list-users
aws iam list-roles
aws iam get-user --user-name alice
aws iam create-user --user-name bob

# ── Output formats ──────────────────────────────────────
aws ec2 describe-instances --output json   # default (full JSON)
aws ec2 describe-instances --output table  # human-readable table
aws ec2 describe-instances --output text   # tab-separated (for scripts)
aws ec2 describe-instances --output yaml   # YAML

# ── Filtering with --query (JMESPath) ───────────────────
aws ec2 describe-instances \
  --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].[InstanceId,State.Name,PublicIpAddress]' \
  --output table

content.filename: Using AWS SDK v3 in your application

content.text: Use --dry-run for destructive EC2 operations. Commands like aws ec2 terminate-instances support --dry-run — they check your permissions and validate the command without actually executing it. Always dry-run before terminating instances or deleting resources you can't easily recover.

questions.question: You have three AWS accounts: personal, staging, and production. How do you switch between them in the CLI?
options: Run 'aws configure' before each command to re-enter credentials
Use named profiles: 'aws configure --profile staging', then 'aws s3 ls --profile staging'
Store all three Access Keys in a single .env file and export the right one
AWS CLI can only be configured for one account at a time
questions.explanation: Named profiles are the correct solution. Run 'aws configure --profile personal', 'aws configure --profile staging', 'aws configure --profile production' once. Then specify '--profile <name>' on any command, or set AWS_PROFILE=staging in your shell. You can also set a profile as default with 'export AWS_DEFAULT_PROFILE=staging'. This keeps all credentials organized and avoids re-entering them each time.

faq.q: Should I use the CLI or the console?
faq.a: Use the console to explore, visualize, and learn — it's great for understanding what resources exist and their relationships. Use the CLI for automation, scripts, and repeatable operations. For production infrastructure, use neither — use Infrastructure as Code (CloudFormation or CDK) so your infrastructure is version-controlled and reproducible.

examples: The AWS CLI's 's3 sync' command is used by millions of teams to deploy static websites: 'aws s3 sync ./dist s3://my-site --delete' uploads new files, updates changed files, and removes deleted files in one command — the foundation of many manual deploy scripts
AWS SDK v3 was redesigned with tree-shaking in mind — instead of importing the entire AWS SDK, you import only the specific service client you need, reducing bundle sizes by 90%+ for Lambda functions
